message:
Now I understand the mechanism. The parser registers allocated structures (privileges, cmndspecs, defaults, members, digests, runas) in a leak list. When `init_parser` is called a second time (with NULL in the fuzz target's cleanup), `free_parse_tree` first frees the parsed policy structures, and then `parser_leak_init` → `parser_leak_free` tries to free the same structures again from the leak list → double-free.

So I need a valid sudoers input that causes the parser to allocate at least one structure that gets registered in the leak list. Let me look at the grammar to understand the minimal valid sudoers syntax. Let me check the test inputs for examples.

<｜｜DSML｜｜tool_calls>
<｜｜DSML｜｜parameter name="command">cd /workspace && cat repo-vul/src-vul/sudo/plugins/sudoers/regress/sudoers/test3.in && echo "---TEST5---" && cat repo-vul/src-vul/sudo/plugins/sudoers/regress/sudoers/test5.in && echo "---TEST11---" && cat repo-vul/src-vul/sudo/plugins/sudoers/regress/sudoers/test11.in</｜｜DSML｜｜parameter>
</｜｜DSML｜｜invoke>
